name: ArtifactsBench
description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation. It evaluates LLMs on interactive visual artifacts by executing generated artifacts in a sandbox, capturing three staged screenshots, and scoring them with checklist-guided multimodal referees. The benchmark contains 1,825 executable queries across nine domains and supports fine-grained analysis of visual fidelity, interaction dynamics, and code quality.
creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated through a multi-stage pipeline designed for diversity, interactivity, provenance, de-duplication, contamination control, and reproducibility. Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified the results. Difficulty was assigned post hoc using aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs. Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist drafted by an LLM and refined by humans. Solvability was validated by collecting candidate solutions from multiple model families and pruning underspecified items.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis, Experiments, Others
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidate tasks were sourced from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control were applied: (i) MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to detect visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed. Difficulty tiers were assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce a 30%/40%/30% split, realized as 559/611/655. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics such as state changes, animations, and responsiveness. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Execution was standardized with headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1024 x 768 resolution and deterministic seeds. Three staged screenshots were captured before, during, and after scripted interaction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were LLM-drafted and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators; the seed was reused as few-shot references to keep difficulty high and rubrics consistent. In human validation, 280 queries and outputs from 6 models were independently scored in a double-blind protocol by multiple front-end engineers, and the final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports calibration and agreement analysis for annotations. A 10% manually curated seed achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators. For human validation, agreement between automated referees and human experts was measured using Pair ACC based on pairwise ranking consistency across model-response pairs. The final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings. The study also analyzed ablations with and without images, multiple screenshots, captions, and answers.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience; annotators in the seed calibration are referred to as annotators, but no further demographics are provided.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results are open-sourced at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io. It also states that dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are released. The paper discusses version stability for the Gemini referee and notes replacing the deprecated Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 with stable Gemini-2.5-Pro does not change conclusions, but no explicit maintenance schedule or deprecation policy for the dataset itself is provided.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The quality filtering prompt explicitly aims to select privacy-free queries and checks that questions avoid sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to provide the community with a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models. The paper argues that evaluating visual fidelity and interactive integrity is important because these qualities are central to user experience in modern applications and affect real-world adoption.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that multimodal LLM referees can suffer from hallucination, prompt sensitivity, limited awareness of engineering/code quality, and version drift. It also notes that different referees may show minor discrepancies on complex interactive tasks, reflecting potential cognitive biases in how different MLLMs interpret long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback.
rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior using a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions such as multi-step workflows or nuanced game physics. The benchmark focuses on the final artifact generated in a single turn and does not assess iterative, agentic refinement, self-debugging, or multi-turn development processes.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifact generation. It is used to evaluate over 30 models with an automated pipeline and dual-referee protocol, enabling leaderboard comparison, fine-grained capability analysis across domains and difficulty tiers, human-alignment validation, and diagnosis of strengths and failure modes in visual fidelity, interaction dynamics, and code quality.
